Made by D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by （签名）

In connection with the agitation of the eighteen
employees of the Lee Dah Lace Weaving Factory, Lane 410,
No.57 Rue Pere Robert, against the decision of the management
to reduce their wages by 30% with effect from October 1,
four of them were dismissed and paid off on October 14.
The remaining employees, who are apprentices, are now
working as usual and have abandoned their agitation against
the reduction in wages.

Subject Nantao Boat Owners - Meeting

Made by D.S. McKeown Forwarded by [签名]

Thirty boat owners of the Nantao Bund held a
meeting in the Ih Ts: Tsung Teashop (一枝春), Tung Ka
Doo, Nantao at 11 a.m. January 21, 1936, and discussed the
refusal of the Chinese Authorities to entrust the boat
owners with the scheme of establishing a steam ferry service
across the Whangpoo between the Nantao Bund and Pootung.
Wong Ah-keng (五阿根), one of the number, presided and
the following resolutions were discussed and passed :-
1. That the Chinese Authorities be requested to take into
consideration the question of the livelihood of boatmen
which will be impaired if the steam ferry service is
operated by persons other than the boatowners.
2. That should the Chinese Authorities persist in their
refusal to allow the boatowners to operate the ferry
service, an appeal be made to the Mayor for relief
measures to be devised to aid the boatmen.
There are altogether one thousand boatowners and
boatmen who obtain a livelihood by conveying passengers
between Tung Ka Doo, Nantao Bund and Pootung. The Bureau of
Public Utility has granted permission to the Shing Nyih Trust
Company to operate a ferry service at Tung Ka Doo, and the
building of a jetty is now in progress.
This scheme has met with strong opposition from
boatowners and boatmen who are of the opinion that if the
ferry service is operated by persons other than themselves,
they will be deprived of them means of livelihood.
The above information was obtained by Agent 31.

At 12.05p.m. 1/5/36 Capt. C. Yost, U.S.M.C., brought to Bubbling Well Station a red flag which at 6.30a.m. had been removed from the roof of "D" Co. U.S.M.C., Ferry Road.

The flag was seen attached to the roof at 6.30a.m. 1/5/36 by 1st. Sgt. King who ordered it to be removed. The flag is of old red bunting patched in several places and 4' by 3'. On the white tape there is "NEW SOUTH WALES; S.M.C., P.W.D." and "牛橋大外兩司" (New South Wales). It was attached to a 7' slat of bamboo fencing with string.

Enquiries by the U.S.M.C. Military Police have not produced any definite information, although it is suspected that U.S. Marines are concerned.

At 3.15p.m. 1/5/36 Sgt. Maj. H. W. Davis, S.V.C. Range Warden at Hongkew Park, came to Bubbling Well Station and identified the flag as a warning marker which had been missing about a fortnight. Since that time various details of the U.S.M.C. have attended the range and it is possible that one of the men stole it.

Sir,
With reference to a letter received at this station on
13.6.36 from the workers of the Tsung Yah Silk Factory, 366
Alcock Road, the translation of which is attached, D.S.I. Tseu
Kwei Sung and the undersigned proceeded to the above factory
at 10 a.m. 13.6.36 when two of the workers who signed the letter
were located and consented to come to the station to allow
further enquiries to be made. When questioned in the presence
of D.S.I. Cumming, the two workers named Sung Fong Hai (沈方海)
and Yih Mau Er (叶毛儿), admitted that the contents of the
letter were incorrect and that actually none of the property
had been removed from the factory on 12.6.36. They stated that
C.D.S. 224( the detective referred to by them in the letter),
arrived at the factory at about 2 p.m. 12.6.36 at the same time
as the factory master's wife, who came accompanied by several
male Chinese with the intention of removing the machinery.
Seeing the detective on the scene, the workers came to the
conclusion that he was there for the express purpose of intimi-
dating them to allow the machinery to be removed.
It was explained to the above named workers that C.D.S. 224
was only there, on the instructions of the undersigned, in a
neutral capacity, to see that no trouble arose between the two
parties which would necessitate police action. On receiving this
explanation the two workers stated that they were satisfied with
same, and later left the station.

Subject Reported outbreak of Cholera in the Sungkiang District.

Made by D.I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by （签名）

With reference to a rumour of outbreak of Cholera
in Sungkiang and vicinity, enquiries on July 3 among the
inhabitants, hospital authorities and Police in this area
disprove any report of an outbreak of Cholera. The record
of the hospital in Sungkiang reveals an increase of 200%
during the month of June in cases of acute Magen-Darmkatarrh
(acute inflammation of stomach and intestine). Other cases
which have come to notice are Typhus abdominatis and Dysentery.
According to the people there, any sign of a serious outbreak of
infectious disease, or epidemic, would be instantly referred
by the Sungkiang Authorities to the Bureau of Health of the
Shanghai City Government for thorough examination in order to
devise immediate preventive measures.
Enquiries were also made among local Roman Catholic
Fathers with likewise negative results.

At 7 a.m. September 9, an affray took place between
a party of workers and staff employees on the premises of the
Hung Shing Hosiery Factory, 221 Rue du Marche, in which sixteen
workers were slightly injured. Further trouble was averted by
the arrival of the French Police. All the employees ceased
work and are still on strike this morning, September 10.
It is learned that the clash arose when the appeal of
the workers for reinstating a female employee, a member of the
Hung Shing Branch of the Knitting Factory Workers' Union, who
was dismissed on September 8 for quarrelling with a non-union
worker, was rejected. In the early morning of September 9, the
dismissed female worker proceeded to the factory with the
intention of resuming work, but was refused admission. On
learning this, her colleagues petitioned the management to
reinstate her or to dismiss the worker who was concerned in the
quarrel. This appeal was rejected with the result that an
affray occurred.
The dispute was reported by the workers to the General
Labour Union and the Bureau of Social Affairs. In the afternoon
of the same day, two officials of the Bureau and the General
Labour Union were sent to the factory for the purpose of
conducting mediation, but no settlement was reached.
This factory employs a total complement of 300 hands,
of whom 200 are reported to be members of the Hung Shing Branch
of the Knitting Factory Workers' Union. Considerable agitation
has been conducted by the workers since the inauguration of
the Branch in June, 1936.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers:

THE HOONG SHING HOSIERY WORKS

Under the cloak of registering workers, the Hoong Shing (鸿兴) Hosiery Works, Rue du Marche, French Concession, suspended operations at the end of June. On the orders of the local Tangpu and other government organs, the management agreed to resume operations on July 20. Unexpectedly, on July 20 the management posted up a circular notice announcing the dismissal of Dung Ih Shing (邓以欣) and 7 other workers all of whom are executives of the labour union. The dismissal gave rise to much indignation among the workers who refused to resume work.
Yesterday afternoon the workers made appeals to Tu Yuet Sun (杜月笙), Loh Ching Sz (陆京士) and Tseu Hsueh Hsiang (周学湘), Acting Chairman of the General Labour Union.
In connection with the labour trouble at the Hoong Shing Hosiery Works, the 2nd District Needle Weaving Trade Workers' Union yesterday submitted a petition to the local Tangpu and other government organs requesting them to order the management to cease dismissing workers without cause. The Union also despatched a telegram to General Chiang Kai Shek, Chairman of the Military Affairs Commission, containing allegations against the Hoong Shing Hosiery Works.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers:

OBJECTION TO EXISTENCE OF A DYEING WORKS NEAR SCHOOLS

There are many schools in the area between Dah Ling Road (大林路) and Kiang Ying Ka (江陰街), Nantao. It is reported that a certain person named Zang Heng Ching (盛杏卿) is planning to establish a "China Industrial Dyeing & Weaving Works" (中國實業染織廠) in that area.
The residents petitioned the Health Bureau, the Social Bureau and the Bureau of Public Safety requesting them to suppress the establishment on the grounds that the quiet of the district would be disturbed by the noise of running machinery, while the fumes given out by the sulphuric acid used in washing and dyeing cloth were harmful to health, especially the health of school children.
On learning of the protests, Zang Heng Ching immediately put up at the gate a sign-board bearing the inscription "The Lih Woong Office" (立丰事務所). He then sent a petition to the official organs denying that he was about to start a dyeing works.

Lih Pao and other local newspapers:

THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE: FURTHER HEARING SET FOR JULY 31

In connection with the Nakayama murder case, the Shanghai First Special District Court at the last hearing announced that the important witnesses in this case would be recalled. The Court has now set the next hearing of the case at 2 p.m. July 31.
Poo Chiao Ying (蒲巧英), an important witness in the case, is at present at Baoyu (寶玉). A detective of the Municipal Police has already been despatched to summon the witness. The officer left here on July 21 with a summons issued by the Court.

南市大林路与江阴街之间区域有许多学校。据报道，一名叫盛杏卿的人计划在该区域建立一家“中国实业染织厂”。
居民们向卫生局、社会局和公安局请愿，要求取缔该工厂，理由是机器运转的噪音会扰乱该地区的宁静，而洗染布料所用的硫酸散发出的烟雾有害健康，尤其是对学童的健康有害。

《大公报》及其他本地报纸：

鸿兴袜厂

关于法租界马当路鸿兴（鴻兴）袜厂的劳资纠纷，社会局于昨日下午2时举行调解会议，当地党部的李维熊以及资方和工人代表出席。该局第三科官员张楚强主持会议。
制定了以下解决争端的措施：-
1) 立即取消资方发布的关于解雇8名工会干部的通告；不解雇这些干部。

3) 工厂于7月20日复工。
4) 等待关于工人待遇的法律调解。
双方同意并签署了这些措施。

《华中日报》及其他本地报纸：

缫丝女工罢工

为抗议增加工资和减少工作时间的要求被拒，虹口区香烟桥新昌及其他两家缫丝厂约1000名女工于7月11日上午7时罢工。随后，该区昌记及其他五家缫丝厂的工人也加入了这一行动。这些缫丝厂的几扇门窗玻璃被损坏和打破。
公安局派遣多名警察镇压工人。第四区缫丝业同业公会的官员也到场调解，并承诺与资方展开谈判。
当局担心不良分子制造骚乱，已指示警察提供保护并采取预防措施。
昨日上午，罢工者复工。资方表示有可能接受将工人工资从40分增加到44分，并将工作时间从上午4:45至下午6:15改为上午5:00至下午5:30的要求。
工人和资方代表今日将前往社会局解决争端。

马当路221号鸿兴袜厂（鴻兴袜廠）的员工最近成立了上海市针织业工人工会的一个分会，办事处设在南市唐家湾洽兴里13号。管理层对工人的活动感到不满，于6月29日关闭了工厂，表面上是因为天气炎热。
7月3日上午，300名工人中的四十人要求复工。然而，管理层要求所有员工在复工前提供担保书并在工厂登记。为了迫使接受他们的要求，工人拒绝离开工厂 premises。代表们被派往当地党部和社会局，目的是向这些当局寻求援助。
下午3点15分，社会局的一名官员访问了工厂，建议工人在调解期间撤离，但他的努力证明无效。
随后，一队法国警察到达现场，逮捕了四名主要煽动者。他们受到警告后被释放。
下午6点，第二区针织工人工会的一名代表来到工厂，张贴告示建议工人在谈判期间离开工厂，随后工人撤离。

THE HOONG SHING HOSIERY WORKS.

On July 3, about 400 workers of the Hoong Shing
Hosiery Works(鸿兴袜厂), Rue du Marche, French Concession,

appeal.

workers, promised to instruct the hosiery workers to resume

The meeting, however, ended without success as the management

union.
The Bureau of Social Affairs will summon

attend an arbitration meeting to be held at 10 a.m. July 6
for the purpose of bringing about an early settlement of
the dispute.

Made by D.S. McKeown Forwarded by （签名）

At 9.30 a.m. to-day, July 31, one Sung Jing-pu
(沈琴波) claiming to represent the 120 ex-workers
of the Ching Foong Dyeing Works, No.1188 Point Road, called
at this office and informed the Police of the labour dispute
existing between the management and ex-workers.
Sung Jing-pu stated that this concern was closed at
the beginning of May, 1936 owing to business depression, and
the property of the firm detained by the First Special
District Court at the request of the creditors. Subsequently
the management negotiated with the creditors and secured
permission to resume business and pay the debts by instalments.
In spite of this agreement, the management sold the
firm to new interests. On July 25, the new proprietor issued
a notice, stating that the factory would be re-opened on
August 1, and that no ex-workers or staff employees would
be re-engaged.
The ex-workers are dissatisfied with this decision,
and in the afternoon of July 28, thirty of them called at
the works with a view to demanding employment but their
demand was rejected (Vide I.R. 29/7/36). Consequently these
ex-workers have requested the Bureau of Social Affairs to
render assistance. It is learned that they intend to visit
the works to-day for the purpose of demanding reinstatement.

今日（7月31日）上午9时30分，一名自称代表宾福路1188号正丰染厂120名前工人的沈琴波来到本办公室，向警方通报了资方与前工人之间存在的劳资纠纷。

TROUBLE WITH
COOLIES IN
HONGKEW PARK.

Further to report on Daily State of 22nd., inst., at
3.30.p.m. 22-8-36 a telephone message was received from Mr.
Repas, Hongkew Park Keeper, stating that he was expecting
trouble in Hongkew Park. A party of Police attended and
ascertained that 50 coolies who had been employed in the
Park during the forenoon had failed to restart work at 2.p.m.
and were gathered in Chapel, opposite to the West Gate of the
Park. Coolie No.10 Lee Mo Dee and about 30 other coolies
casually employed in the Park had proceeded during the
morning to the Head Office of the P.W.D. and Coolie No.10
together with Coolie No.79 Zung Kyung San had interviewed
Mr. Kerr, Supt. of Parks and Open Spaces and complained that
Coolie No.10 had been assaulted by Mr. Repas on the 21st.
inst, and that this was the only reason for ceasing work.
They made no demands. Mr. Kerr told them to return to work
and that they would receive full pay for the day and that he
would enquire into their complaint. They returned to the
Park to work but allege Mr. Repas informed them that they
would not be required till Monday the 24th. inst. Mr. Repas
states that when they returned he told them they could start
and receive full pay for the day but instead he alleges they
intimidated 50 other coolies working in the Park and they too
ceased work. Foreman Kuh Kung Kung corroborated the state-
ments of Coolies No.10 and 79, thus contradicting that of
Mr. Repas.
Mr. Kerr was present and after negotiations Coolie
No.10 was severely cautioned re any attempt of intimidation
and was instructed to tell the other coolies to report for
work on the morning of the 23rd. inst, and to leave the
matter of the alleged assault to be dealt with by Mr. Kerr.
Coolie No.10 agreed to this and the few coolies gathered
opposite the West Gate of the Park dispersed without causing
any trouble.

继本月22日每日状况报告之后，1936年8月22日下午3时30分，接到虹口公园看守 Repas 先生的电话留言，称他预计虹口公园会发生麻烦。一队警察前往现场，查明上午在公园受雇的50名苦力未在下午2时复工，而是聚集在公园西门对面的教堂内。10号苦力 Lee Mo Dee 和约30名其他在公园临时受雇的苦力，于上午前往工务局 (P.W.D.) 总部，10号苦力与79号苦力 Zung Kyung San 会见了公园及空地总监 Kerr 先生，投诉称10号苦力于本月21日遭到 Repas 先生殴打，并称这是他们停工的唯一原因。他们没有提出任何要求。Kerr 先生让他们回去工作，并表示他们将获得当天的全额工资，且他会调查他们的投诉。他们返回公园工作，但声称 Repas 先生告知他们，直到本月24日（星期一）才需要他们上班。Repas 先生称，当他们回来时，他告诉他们可以开始工作并获得当天的全额工资，但他们反而恐吓了公园里工作的其他50名苦力，导致这些人也停止了工作。领班 Kuh Kung Kung 证实了10号和79号苦力的陈述，从而反驳了 Repas 先生的说法。

Sir,
At 3 p.m. on the 2-11-36 a male Chinese named Poo Ying Woo
(浦英華) 20, Zangchow, employed at the above concern came to
the station and reported that at about 2.30 p.m. even date the
employer Zung Shing Kwei (朱信煒) had assaulted him.
Enquiries made by C.D.C. 98, C.D.C. 277 and the undersigned
ascertained that the above concern employs 20 workers each re-
ceiving $2.00 per month salary. Of this $2.00 Zung Shing Kwei
keeps $1.50 on the understanding that if any of the workers re-
quired money to buy personal effects or return to the country
he would give them the amount due to them. About one week ago
Zung Shing Kwei informed the workers that if they increased the
out-put of nails he would pay them extra money. Today the workers,
led by Poo Ying Woo, demanded the promised increase of pay, but
when Zung Shing Kwei informed them that as they had not increased
their out-put they would not receive the promised increase, Poo
Ying Woo then became very abusive and insolent which angered
Zung to the extent that he struck Poo with his hand on the mouth
causing it to bleed slightly.
The workers stated that if Zung gave them the whole of their
wages each month and not keep the $1.50 they would return to
work and on Zung agreeing to their request work was resumed.
Poo Ying Woo stated that he did not wish to take action
against Zung, but requested the police to caution him re assault-
ing his employees.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,

Subject Labour situation at the Shanghai No.6 Mill (woollen factory) at
45 Chinchow Road.

Made by D.S.I. Crighton Forwarded by [签名] Inspt. O. i/c

Sir,

At 1 p.m. 10/11/36 information was received from the above
mill to the effect that they were having trouble with workers
of all departments of the mill. D.S.I. Crighton and J.D.S. 42
Uecka immediately proceeded to this factory, where on arrival
enquiries revealed that at 12noon all departments had ceased
work for purpose of partaking of their mid-day meal and that
instead of commencing work at 12.30 p.m. they refused to do so.
The management then called together several of the foremen
who informed them that the workers were making the following
demands:-
(1) That the management revive the reward for non-absence.
(2) That the management make a rice allowance for the workers.
These demands were, prior to 1931 issued to all workers
employed by Japanese mills, but owing to the business depression
were cut out.
In reply to these demands the management gave the understand-
ing that they would be given due consideration and requested
workers to continue.
Work was commenced at 1 p.m. and since then the general
situation in this mill has remained normal.
At 6 p.m. 10/11/36 the night shift consisting 70 workers
paraded for duty as usual, and nothing of an outstanding nature
has since taken place.

I am, Sir,

Your obedient servant,
[签名]
for D. S. I. Crighton

1936年11月10日下午1时，收到上述工厂传来的消息，称该厂所有部门的工人均出现麻烦。副侦探长克莱顿和日籍侦探员42号宇惠卡（Uecka）立即前往该工厂，到达后经查询得知，中午12时所有部门停止工作去吃午饭，但在下午12时30分本应开始工作时，他们拒绝开工。随后管理层召集了几名工头，工头告知他们工人提出了以下要求：

这些要求在1931年之前曾发给所有受雇于日本工厂的工人，但由于商业萧条而被取消。

Date June 30, 1937.
Subject Shanghai Municipality Galvanized Ironsheet Shop
Owners' Association - disturbance during inaugural
meeting in Ningpo Fellow Countrymen' Association.
Made by D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien Forwarded by J. Loyne S.S.I.

At 3.30 p.m. June 28, the Shanghai Municipality
Galvanized Ironsheet Shop Owners' Association, No.89 Heng
Meu Li, Boulevard de Montigny, which is in possession of
permit No.596 issued by the Bureau of Social Affairs, held
an inaugural meeting in the Ningpo Fellow Countrymen's
Association, 480 Yu Ya Ching Road. About 300 persons,
including representatives from the local Chinese Chamber of
Commerce, the local Tangpu and the Bureau of Social Affairs
were present, and Mr. Dzien Yung-nyi (錢永宜), owner of
the Yung Chong (永昌) Galvanized Ironsheet Shop, Miao Deu
(苗頭), Chapei, and principal of the Yoong Tsing (勇進)
Primary School, 36 Chung An Li (長安里), Tiendong Road,
presided over the meeting.

When the meeting passed the revised regulations of
the association and the scale of membership fees, one of the
promoters of the association named Tsang Ching-loong (張金龍),
who is on the list of candidates for the executive committee,
had a quarrel with two of the attendance, whom he approached
with the request to have him elected member of the executive
committee. The majority of the attendance became indignant
over this action on the part of Tsang and shouted "beat him"
thereupon Tsang took refuge on the platform. Through the
intervention of the members of the presidium, he was allowed
to go. The meeting then dispersed as more than half of the
attendance left the premises during the disturbance.

Tsang Ching-loong is the owner of the Tsang Van-
tsung Galvanized Ironsheet Shop, opposite the Yangchow Guild,
Poo Zoen Road, Chapei.

事由 上海市镀锌铁皮店业主联合会 - 在宁波同乡会举行成立大会期间发生骚乱。
呈报人：副侦探长施思坚 转呈人：J·洛恩 高级副督察。

6月28日下午3时30分，持有社会局颁发的第596号许可证、位于蒙脱尼路（Boulevard de Montigny）恒美里89号的上海市镀锌铁皮店业主联合会，在虞洽卿路480号宁波同乡会举行成立大会。约300人出席，包括当地华人总商会、当地塘浦和社会局的代表，会议由闸北苗头永昌镀锌铁皮店店主、田东路长安里36号勇进小学校长钱永宜（Dzien Yung-nyi）主持。

当会议通过修订后的协会章程和会费标准时，协会发起人之一、执行委员会候选人名单上的张金龙（Tsang Ching-loong），向两名与会者提出请求，希望当选为执行委员会委员，由此发生争吵。大多数与会者对张的这种行为感到愤怒，高喊“打他”，随后张躲到主席台上。经主席团成员干预，他被允许离开。由于骚乱期间超过一半的与会者离开了会场，会议随即解散。

张金龙是闸北蒲淞路扬州会馆对面的张万宗镀锌铁皮店的店主。
